Introductory Discourse
Karuṇāsītalahadayaṃ, paññāpajjotavihatamohatamaṃ;
With a mind cooled by supreme compassion, having dispelled the darkness of delusion with the lamp of wisdom;
Sanarāmaralokagaruṃ, vande sugataṃ gativimuttaṃ.
I bow my head to the Blessed One (sugataṃ), the Teacher of the world of devas and humans, who is freed from destinations.
Buddhopi buddhabhāvaṃ, bhāvetvā ceva sacchikatvā ca;
The Buddha, having developed the state of being a Buddha and having personally realized it,
Yaṃ upagato gatamalaṃ, vande tamanuttaraṃ dhammaṃ .
I bow to that unsurpassed Dhamma, which he attained, untainted.
Sugatassa orasānaṃ, puttānaṃ mārasenamathanānaṃ;
To the sons of the Blessed One, the crushers of the army of Māra,
Aṭṭhannampi samūhaṃ, sirasā vande ariyasaṅghaṃ .
I bow my head to the assembly of the eight kinds of Noble Saṅgha.
Iti me pasannamatino, ratanattayavandanāmayaṃ puññaṃ;
Thus, the merit from this homage to the Triple Gem, of me with a clear mind,
Yaṃ suvihatantarāyo, hutvā tassānubhāvena.
May all dangers be dispelled by its power.
Dīghassa dīghasuttaṅkitassa, nipuṇassa āgamavarassa ;
Of the Long (Dīgha) Nikāya, marked by long discourses, and of the profound Excellent Collection (āgamavarassa);
Buddhānubuddhasaṃvaṇṇitassa, saddhāvahaguṇassa.
Praised by the Buddha and his disciples, carrying the quality of faith.
Atthappakāsanatthaṃ, aṭṭhakathā ādito vasisatehi;
To illuminate the meaning, the Commentary (aṭṭhakathā) was originally recited by the five hundred elders,
Pañcahi yā saṅgītā, anusaṅgītā ca pacchāpi.
And subsequently recited again.
Sīhaḷadīpaṃ pana ābhatātha, vasinā mahāmahindena;
Brought to the island of Sihala by the master, the Great Mahinda,
Ṭhapitā sīhaḷabhāsāya, dīpavāsīnamatthāya.
It was established in the Sinhala language for the benefit of the island's inhabitants.
Apanetvāna tatohaṃ, sīhaḷabhāsaṃ manoramaṃ bhāsaṃ;
Discarding that Sinhala language, I shall express the meaning in the delightful Magadha language,
Tantinayānucchavikaṃ, āropento vigatadosaṃ.
Which conforms to the Pāli text and is free of errors.
Samayaṃ avilomento, therānaṃ theravaṃsapadīpānaṃ;
Without opposing the tradition of the Elders who are the beacons of the Elder lineage,
Sunipuṇavinicchayānaṃ, mahāvihāre nivāsīnaṃ.
Who reside in the Great Monastery and possess profoundly analytical insights.
Hitvā punappunāgatamatthaṃ, atthaṃ pakāsayissāmi;
Setting aside the meaning that has been repeated again and again, I shall explain the meaning,
Sujanassa ca tuṭṭhatthaṃ, ciraṭṭhitatthañca dhammassa.
For the joy of good people and for the long-standing of the Dhamma.
Sīlakathā dhutadhammā, kammaṭṭhānāni ceva sabbāni;
Virtue, ascetic principles, and all meditations,
Cariyāvidhānasahito, jhānasamāpattivitthāro.
Accompanied by the conduct and the detailed jhānas and attainments.
Sabbā ca abhiññāyo, paññāsaṅkalananicchayo ceva;
All direct knowledges and the decision through the synthesis of wisdom,
Khandhadhātāyatanindriyāni, ariyāni ceva cattāri.
The aggregates, elements, sense bases, faculties, and the four Noble Truths.
Saccāni paccayākāradesanā, suparisuddhanipuṇanayā;
The Truths, the exposition of conditions, the pure and profound methods,
Avimuttatantimaggā, vipassanā bhāvanā ceva.
The path of the Pāli text not left behind, and insight meditation,
Iti pana sabbaṃ yasmā, visuddhimagge mayā suparisuddhaṃ;
Since all this has been perfectly explained by me in the Visuddhimagga,
Vuttaṃ tasmā bhiyyo, na taṃ idha vicārayissāmi.
Therefore, I will not explain it further here.
‘‘ Majjhe visuddhimaggo , esa catunnampi āgamānañhi;
‘‘ Standing in the middle, the Visuddhimagga is common to all four collections;’’
Ṭhatvā pakāsayissati, tattha yathā bhāsitaṃ atthaṃ ’’.
‘‘ It will clarify the meaning as it has been spoken therein.’’
Icceva kato tasmā, tampi gahetvāna saddhimetāya;
Because it was composed with the intention that it would clarify the meaning therein by standing in the middle of the four collections, therefore, having taken that as well with faith,
Aṭṭhakathāya vijānatha, dīghāgamanissitaṃ atthanti.
Understand the meaning relying on the Dīgha Nikāya through this commentary.
Nidānakathā
Introductory Story
Tattha dīghāgamo nāma sīlakkhandhavaggo, mahāvaggo, pāthikavaggoti vaggato tivaggo hoti;
There, the Dīgha Nikāya consists of three divisions: the Sīlakkhandhavagga, the Mahāvagga, and the Pāthikavagga;
suttato catuttiṃsasuttasaṅgaho.
it is a collection of thirty-four discourses.
Tassa vaggesu sīlakkhandhavaggo ādi, suttesu brahmajālaṃ .
Among those divisions, the Sīlakkhandhavagga is the first; among the discourses, the Brahmajāla is the first.
Brahmajālassāpi ‘‘ evaṃ me sutan ’’ tiādikaṃ āyasmatā ānandena paṭhamamahāsaṅgītikāle vuttaṃ nidānamādi.
The introductory story of the Brahmajāla, beginning with 'Thus have I heard', was spoken by Venerable Ānanda at the time of the First Great Council.
